transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we really appreciate you carving out time this afternoon. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Tara (Aurelia): Hey Tara here, Head of MLOps — thanks Samir.
[00:13] Diego (Aurelia): Diego, platform eng.
[00:15] Priya (Aurelia): Priya, product.
[00:18] Evan (Aurelia): Evan, security.
[00:20] Lena (Redwood CSM): Lena here, I'll be your CSM for the pilot.
[00:24] Marcus (Redwood SE): Marcus, SE — I'll run the network/bench stuff.
[00:28] Samir: Awesome. Agenda is short: run through the onboarding runbook, nail down networking and SSO asks, agree pilot metrics, and confirm immediate deliverables. If anything else pops up we can table it.
[00:42] Priya: Sounds good. Our timeline — we want the pilot live early December, ideally a two-week smoke + performance window, then evaluate for Dedicated in Q1.
[00:50] Samir: Great — that's tight but doable. Lena, we'll account for ramp.
[00:54] Lena: Yep we'll prioritize the access and onboarding checklist.
[00:58] [01:02] Marcus: Quick question on the VPC options — do you plan to go Redwood Private (VPC) or start hosted and then move to dedicated?
[01:10] Diego: We prefer VPC from day one for data path control. Legal wants network separation.
[01:14] Evan: Also need KMS integration—customer-managed keys for inference logs retention.
[01:18] Samir: Okay VPC-first. Marcus, we have a standard peering template but we need Diego's CIDR and routing expectations.
[01:26] Diego: We'll share the network diagram after the call. Expect 10.0.0.0/16 internal; we'll probably do a dedicated subnet for inference.
[01:33] Marcus: Perfect. We'll send a peering checklist and a stub terraform snippet.
[01:36] Priya: On pilot success criteria — what do we need to provide from product to make this a meaningful test?
[01:41] Lena: Usually a set of representative prompts, a clear latency SLO (P95/P99), and error tolerance. Also business metrics like conversion uplift or throughput targets help.
[01:49] Priya: For us, P95 < 300ms is aspirational, but realistic P95 around 400ms if needed. Throughput target is ~120 reqs/min at peak.
[01:58] Samir: Noted. We should run a small benchmark to validate those numbers. Marcus can provision a test endpoint with load harness.
[02:06] Marcus: Yeah I'll spin up a sandbox endpoint with the same model stack and run a 1-week profile if you can provide typical payload sizes.
[02:13] Diego: We'll export the last 2 weeks of traffic histogram — payloads are usually 1-2k tokens.
[02:18] Evan: Security requirements — SOC2 scope is important; we also need audit logs to be retained for 90 days and encrypted in transit and at rest. KMS integration is a must.
[02:29] Samir: Redwood supports customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated; for hosted APIs we have ARK (typo: API key?) rotation options, but for VPC we'll wire to your KMS. I'll follow up with details.
[02:40] [02:45] Priya: One concern from the team — does Redwood keep any PII in logs? We need to understand retention and redaction.
[02:52] Lena: We can configure token-level logging and redact fields. For Private deployment you control logs; for hosted we can set retention and offer field redaction patterns, but we'll get the security doc over.
[03:03] Samir: I'll attach the security playbook and SOC2 checklist after the call.
[03:07] [03:12] Diego: About SSO — we use Okta and want SCIM for provisioning. Can Redwood support automated group sync?
[03:18] Marcus: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. We'll need metadata and which attributes you want mapped.
[03:24] Evan: Also need role-based access control — devs vs ops vs auditors.
[03:28] Lena: We'll include an RBAC matrix template in the runbook.
[03:31] [03:36] Samir: On the runbook timeline — propose: we send a draft onboarding runbook today, customer reviews by Friday, network walkthrough next Tuesday, and benchmark provisioning by mid-next week. Sound OK?
[03:47] Priya: That timeline works for us.
[03:49] Evan: Fine.
[03:50] [04:00] Diego: One technical nit — model variant. We'd like to start on an open LLM variant comparable to gpt-ish (transcription glitch: gpt-ish) but keep option to swap to smaller quantized variant if cost spikes. How easy is swapping models mid-pilot?
[04:14] Marcus: Very straightforward — we can create model aliases and do a canary switch. Latency/cost tradeoffs are visible in the console. We'll recommend quantized variants for cost optimization if quality holds.
[04:25] Samir: We also have automatic fallback policies if a variant fails; will outline in the runbook.
[04:30] [04:34] Priya: On observability — do we get token-level cost breakdowns and per-prompt tracing?
[04:39] Lena: Yes, the Console exposes token-level costs, model-level latency histograms, and trace links you can export. We'll set up dashboard templates.
[04:47] [04:55] Priya: Good. Also, does Redwood have eval hooks to catch regressions as we change prompts?
[04:58] Samir: Yes — Redwood Optimize has prompt-set backed quality monitors; we can register a few baseline prompts and get alerts on regressions.
[05:06] Evan: For compliance we need a paper trail of changes — audit events for model swaps and config changes.
[05:11] Marcus: Audit logs include user, timestamp, before/after config. We'll show samples.
[05:17] [05:30] Samir: Let's talk pilot traffic shape once more — Diego, you said 120 reqs/min peak, payload 1-2k tokens. Anything else? Burst behavior?
[05:40] Diego: We'll have short spikes up to 300 reqs/min for 30-60s during business hours, so batching and autoscale behavior matters.
[05:48] Marcus: Good to know. We'll recommend autoscale thresholds and a warmup plan.
[05:52] [06:00] Priya: What's the expected ETA to get test credentials and an endpoint?
[06:04] Marcus: If we get network bits and SAML later this week, I can provision a sandbox endpoint within 48 hours.
[06:09] Samir: I can push the runbook and the onboarding checklist within a day.
[06:13] [06:20] Evan: One more — where do we stand on data residency? Our legal wants EU-only for certain datasets.
[06:26] Samir: We support region pinning for both hosted and Private; for EU-only we'll propose a dedicated region host or Private. We'll include region options in the runbook.
[06:35] [06:40] Priya: Pricing question — rough estimate for pilot cost so we can budget?
[06:44] Samir: For the pilot duration (2 weeks, expected tokens X) we can send an estimate after Marcus runs the sample benchmark. For Dedicated, we'll share reserved capacity options.
[06:53] [07:00] Diego: Can you also share a minimal RBAC set we should create in Okta so we can map groups?
[07:05] Lena: Yes — we'll include an Okta mapping example and minimum groups (admin, dev, ops, auditor).
[07:10] [07:18] Priya: Ok one more ops question: incident escalation — who do we contact for P1 vs P2?
[07:23] Samir: We'll include a support matrix: SLAs for Dedicated, on-call rotation, and escalation path with phone and pager. For pilot we'll have a named SE and CSM and an on-call contact.
[07:34] [07:45] Marcus: I want to highlight the benchmark plan: we'll do a cold-start and warm-start profile, measure P50/P95/P99, and record throughput. Expect results in 48 hours after harness runs.
[07:56] Diego: Great.
[08:00] [08:18] Priya: Anything else?
[08:20] Evan: A quick note — audit for encryption algorithms (AES-256) and HSM/KMS product — do you support AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault?
[08:30] Samir: Yes to both. For on-prem private deployments we also support HSM integrations. We'll collect your KMS ARN.
[08:38] [08:45] Priya: Perfect.
[08:48] Lena: I'll follow up with the onboarding calendar invite: network walkthrough (Marcus + Diego + Evan) and a separate SSO session.
[08:56] Samir: To recap — Redwood sends runbook + security doc; Marcus provisions sandbox after network details; Aurelia provides SAML metadata, KMS requirements, traffic histograms, and the pilot prompt set.
[09:10] Priya: Confirmed.
[09:12] Diego: Confirmed.
[09:14] Evan: Confirmed.
[09:17] Samir: Great — we'll target the benchmark week starting Nov 22. Is that align with your calendar?
[09:22] Priya: Yes that works.
[09:24] Lena: I'll send the invites and action-item list.
[09:28] Samir: Any final questions?
[09:31] [09:40] Priya: None from me. Thanks everyone.
[09:43] Samir: Thanks all. We'll follow up via email with artifacts: runbook.docx (link), network-peering-template.tf (link), security-playbook.pdf (link).
[09:55] [09:59] Diego: Thanks.
[10:00] [10:30] *call ends*
